notice: RN bank batch 136: Maternity case studies: fetal monitoring on oxytocin, cord prolapse, preterm labor and the labor epidural. Written as part of a full NGN case study to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 20 November 2026. See REVIEW-LOG.md.

questions.stem: Highlight the findings that require immediate action.

rationale.correct: Tachysystole with late decelerations and minimal variability is a Category II to III pattern.
references: Maternal-newborn nursing texts (e.g. Perry; Lowdermilk)

questions.stem: Complete the sentence by choosing from the lists of options.

content.template: The nurse's first action is to {{b1}}, because {{b2}}.

options.text: stop the oxytocin infusion
increase the oxytocin to speed birth
prepare for an epidural
perform a cervical exam
frequent strong contractions reduce placental blood flow
the cervix is not dilating
the client is tired
the FHR is normal

rationale.correct: Stop the oxytocin first.
references: Maternal-newborn nursing texts (e.g. Perry; Lowdermilk)
Nursing pharmacology texts (e.g. Lehne; McCuistion) and the drug's prescribing information

questions.stem: Place the intrauterine resuscitation steps in order after stopping the oxytocin.

rationale.correct: Reposition, fluids, oxygen if needed, tocolytic if needed, then notify and document.
references: Maternal-newborn nursing texts (e.g. Perry; Lowdermilk)
Written as part of a full NGN case study to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 20 November 2026.

questions.stem: The nurse calls the provider using SBAR. Which statements belong in the report? Select all that apply.

options.text: "Situation: recurrent late decelerations on oxytocin."
"Background: G1 at 41 weeks, induction, 5 cm."
"Assessment: tachysystole; oxytocin off, bolus given."
"Recommendation: please come to evaluate now."
"I think the baby is probably fine, so there is no rush to come."
"The resident ordered too much oxytocin again, like last week."

rationale.correct: SBAR gives a clear, factual report with a request.
references: NCSBN National Guidelines for Nursing Delegation; LaCharity, Prioritization, Delegation & Assignment
Maternal-newborn nursing texts (e.g. Perry; Lowdermilk)

questions.stem: At 30 minutes, for each finding, indicate whether it shows recovery or needs follow-up.

rows.text: Recurrent late decelerations with absent variability

rationale.correct: Recovery allows the induction to restart carefully; absent variability with lates means emergency birth.

questions.stem: Complete the sentence by choosing from the lists of options.

content.template: The nurse's first action is to {{b1}}, while {{b2}}.

options.text: lift the presenting part off the cord with a gloved hand
push the cord back into the uterus
leave the room to call for help
start oxytocin
calling for help and preparing for emergency cesarean
waiting for full dilation
documenting the event first
removing the hand to check the FHR

rationale.correct: Relieve compression and prepare for immediate birth.

perOption.b1:b: Causes spasm and is not done.

questions.stem: Which other actions should the nurse anticipate? Select all that apply.

options.text: Knee-chest or steep Trendelenburg position
Cover exposed cord with warm moist gauze
Fill the bladder with saline if ordered
Keep the hand in place until birth
Massage the cord gently to restore its pulsation
Ask the client to push hard with the next contraction

rationale.correct: Positioning, cord protection and continued elevation.

questions.stem: Magnesium sulfate 4 g IV loading dose over 20 minutes is ordered. The bag contains 4 g in 100 mL. At what rate should the nurse set the pump? Record your answer in mL/hr.

rationale.correct: 100 mL over 20 minutes = 100 / (20/60) = 300 mL/hr.
references: Nursing pharmacology texts (e.g. Lehne; McCuistion) and the drug's prescribing information

Encourage oral fluids to flush it out

Check the FHR after each contraction
Watch for bulging of the perineum and crowning
Tell the client to push continuously between contractions
Push hard on the top of the uterus to speed birth

caseStudies.title: Oxytocin induction with tachysystole and late decelerations

exhibits.title: Labor and delivery, 41 weeks
exhibits.body: A 30-year-old client (G1 P0) is being induced for post-term pregnancy. Oxytocin was increased to 12 milliunits/min an hour ago. The cervix is 5 cm dilated.

rows.label: Decelerations
cells: Gradual drops starting after each contraction peak, returning after it ends

exhibits.title: Labor and delivery, 38 weeks
exhibits.body: A 27-year-old client (G3 P2) with polyhydramnios and a high, unengaged fetal head has a sudden gush of fluid when the membranes rupture. The FHR drops at once.

rows.label: Vaginal exam
cells: A pulsating cord felt in the vagina

caseStudies.title: Preterm labor with tocolysis and magnesium

exhibits.title: Triage, 29 weeks
exhibits.body: A 22-year-old client (G1 P0) at 29 weeks has low back ache and tightening every 6 minutes for 3 hours. The client had a urinary tract infection last week that was not treated.

caseStudies.title: Labor epidural with hypotension and the stages of labor

exhibits.title: Labor and delivery
exhibits.body: A 31-year-old client (G2 P1) in active labor at 6 cm requests an epidural. The nurse gave a 500 mL lactated Ringer's bolus before placement. Fifteen minutes after the epidural is started, the client says, "I feel dizzy and sick."
